# IgG4-RD Registry Study 

The IgG4-RD Registry is an anonymised database of patients with IgG4-RD.

This European database was set up with the aim of establishing the epidemiology, clinical course, resonse to treatment and prognoisis attributed to IgG4-RD.

results.title: National Registry of IgG4-RD in China
results.text:
# National Registry of IgG4-RD in China

- NCT ID: NCT03023371
- Official title: National Registry of IgG4-RD in China
- Organization: Peking Union Medical College Hospital
- Status: RECRUITING
- Start date: 2016-12
- Completion date: 2026-12
- Primary completion: 2026-12
- Lead sponsor: Peking Union Medical College Hospital

## Summary

The aim of this study is to establish a nation-wide cohort study of IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) in China.

Methods: All the patients fulfilling diagnostic criteria of IgG4-RD (2011) would be enrolled from multi-centers around China. A online database system has been established.

Endpoints: The primary endpoint is to investigate the clinical manifestations of Chinese IgG4-RD patients; the secondary endpoints including the demographic features,laboratory characteristics, immunological tests, imaging and pathological features, in addition, the treatment and prognosis of the disease.

## Detailed Description

This is a multicenter registry study of IgG4-RD patients. Newly diagnosed IgG4-RD patients will be recruited from allover the China. Inclusion criteria: patients with definite, probable, or possible IgG4-RD according to the 2011 comprehensive diagnostic criteria for IgG4-RD will be recruited. Exclusion criteria: patients with malignancy or other autoimmune diseases are excluded.

The data will be uploaded through the platform of Chinese Rheumatology Information Platform. Demographic data, initial symptoms, disease duration, history of allergy, and physical examination, organ involvements, laboratory findings, radiological and pathological results, as well as treatment, side effects will be recorded.

This study was approved by the Medical Ethics Committee of PUMCH (Beijing, China). All patients will signe informed consent.

Statistical Analysis: All parameters are described in the standard summary statistics, including mean, standard deviation, minimum, and maximum. All statistical analyses will be performed by SPSS.

Endpoints: The primary endpoint is to investigate the organ involvements of Chinese IgG4-RD patients. The secondary endpoints including the demographic features,laboratory characteristics, immunological tests, imaging and pathological features, in addition, the treatment and prognosis of the disease.

## Conditions

- IgG4-Related Disease

## Keywords

- Registry; cohort study; IgG4-related disease

## Study Design

- Study type: OBSERVATIONAL
- Enrollment: 900 (ESTIMATED)
- Observational model: COHORT

## Primary Outcomes

### Organ involvements of Chinese IgG4-RD patients

To calculate the percentage of organ involvements in at least 900 patients.

Time frame: 5 years

## Secondary Outcomes

### Response rate of glucocorticoids and immunosuppressants on IgG4-RD in China

Time frame: 5 years

### Relapse rate of IgG4-RD patients in China

Time frame: 5 years

### The correlation between baseline disease activities and relapse rate.

Time frame: 5 years

### The incidence rate of tumor in IgG4 related disease patients in China.

Time frame: 5 years

### Ten year survival rate of patients with IgG4 related disease in China.

Time frame: 10 years

### The imaging features of involved organs.

Time frame: 3 years

### The sensitivity and specificity of IgG4 positive plasma cells in pathological diagnosis of IgG4 related disease.

Time frame: 3 years

## Eligibility

- Sex: ALL
- Healthy volunteers: no
- Standard ages: CHILD, ADULT, OLDER_ADULT

Inclusion Criteria:

* Conforming to the diagnostic criteria of IgG4-RD (2011);

Exclusion Criteria:

* Excluding other mimicing IgG4-RD, including tumors, vasculitis and sarcoidosis.

## Locations

1 location(s) across 1 country

- Peking Union Medical College Hospital, Beijing, China [RECRUITING]

results.title: POS0499 CARE SITUATION OF GERMAN PATIENTS WITH IgG4-RELATED DISEASE - FIRST EXCERPTS FROM THE GERMAN LüRIgG-4 REGISTRY
results.author: Thea Thiele, Marc Phillipp Silchmüller, L. Risser, Lukas Graalmann, S. Hirsch, Torsten Witte, et al.
results.text:
# POS0499 CARE SITUATION OF GERMAN PATIENTS WITH IgG4-RELATED DISEASE - FIRST EXCERPTS FROM THE GERMAN LüRIgG-4 REGISTRY

Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases. Published: 2025-06-01. 0 citations.

## Abstract

Background: IgG4-related diseases (IgG4-RD) are rare fibroinflammatory diseases with a highly variable clinical course [1, 2]. Recently, there have been new insights into epidemiological data [3] but a structured collection of IgG4-RD cases in Germany is currently lacking. To obtain a clearer picture of the epidemiological data and the care situation of German individuals affected by IgG4-RD, the registry study ‘local and nationwide registry for IgG4-RD' (short title: LüRIgG-4) has been established. Currently, Hannover and Augsburg are among the participating study centers. Objectives: In this first excerpt from the German LüRIgG4 registry we aimed to gain a better understanding of the current care situation, Patient related outcomes (PRO) and future needs of patients with IgG4-RD. Methods: In the rheumatology outpatient clinics of Hannover Medical School and University Hospital of Augsburg, all patients with IgG4-RD and their physicians filled a standardized questionnaire after giving consent for the LürIgG4 registry between September 09 th 2024 and January 14 th 2025. In addition to demographic data, questions about initial referral, the medical institution and specialty confirming and diagnosing the IgG4-RD, quality of life and need for information about IgG4-RD both expressed on a visual analogue scale (VAS) were evaluated for this analysis. Results: A total of n=28 patients with balanced gender ratio that had previously been diagnosed with IgG4-RD were included in this analysis. Patients' characteristics regarding the IgG4-RD are shown in Table 1. 60.7% initially consulted their primary care doctor with the symptoms that later led to diagnosis of IgG4-RD. 42.9 % were referred to a specialist with a suspected malignant disease. In 67,9% rheumatologists were the most frequent specialists finally diagnosing the IgG4-RD. Details are shown in Figure 1 A and B. 10.7 % of patients live 100 km or further, 21.4 % 50-100 km and 67.9% less than 50 km away from their treatment centre. On a VAS of 0-10 the mean quality of life was stated as 5.78 (range 0-10, 0 being no disease related impaired quality of life to 10 maximum disease related impairment of QOL). Patients that had been suspected to have malignant disease prior to diagnosis tended to report a worse disease related quality of life of 6.5 compared to 5.1 in patients without suspected malignancy. None of the participants had ever heard of IgG4-RD prior to diagnosis and a large majority wished for more information about their disease. On a VAS from 0 (wish for no more information) to 10 (maximum wish for information) the mean value was 7.08. Most frequently named sources of information were internet and the specialist doctor e.g the rheumatologist. Conclusion: The impact of a suspected malignant tumor before IgG4-RD was diagnosed or during the course of IgG4-RD is sustainable. These patients tended to report a greater impairment of quality of life due to their IgG4-RD than patients without suspected tumor. Good training and targeted information campaigns for general practitioners in Germany could help improve the immediate care situation. In addition, the thirst for information on the part of patients is no less. Table 1. Patients characteristics of the current LüRIgG4-cohort Figure 1A and B: Medical disciplines involved in the care, first (A) and second (B) contact. Arthritis Rheumatol, 2020. 72 (1): p. 7-19. [2] Perugino, C.A. and J.H. Stone, IgG4-related disease: an update on pathophysiology and implications for clinical care. Nat Rev Rheumatol, 2020. 16 (12): p. 702-714. [3] Wallace, Z.S., et al., Incidence,

results.title: Vorstellung der multizentrischen Längsschnittstudie „Lokales und überregionales Register für IgG4-assoziierte Erkrankungen (LüRIgG-4)“
results.author: Felix Müller, Thea Thiele, Frank Krämer, Désirée Dunstheimer, Torsten Witte, Matthias Wahle
results.text:
# Vorstellung der multizentrischen Längsschnittstudie „Lokales und überregionales Register für IgG4-assoziierte Erkrankungen (LüRIgG-4)“

Aktuelle Rheumatologie. Published: 2025-07-31. 1 citation.

## Abstract

Zusammenfassung Die IgG4-assoziierte Erkrankung (IgG4-RD) ist eine seltene, komplexe und häufig unterdiagnostizierte fibro-inflammatorische Systemerkrankung. Um das Verständnis und die Behandlung dieser Erkrankung zu verbessern, wurde die multizentrische Längsschnittstudie „LüRIgG-4“ zur Erfassung und strukturierten Untersuchung der IgG4-RD etabliert. Startschuss für die prospektive Registerstudie stellte eine retrospektive Fallanalyse der IgG4-RD-Fälle am Universitätsklinikum Augsburg (UKA) dar. LüRIgG-4 kann sowohl prävalente als auch inzidente Fälle einschließen. Die Dateneingabe erfolgt über das elektronische Case Report Form (eCRF), das eine strukturierte digitale, pseudonymisierte Datenerfassung ermöglicht. LüRIgG-4 hat zum Ziel, lokal auftretende IgG4-RD Fälle strukturiert zu erfassen, retrospektiv und prospektiv zu analysieren und die Daten überregional zusammenzuführen. Ziel ist eine verlässliche und breite Datengrundlage zu schaffen, um die Qualität der Versorgung bei diesem seltenen Krankheitsbild nachhaltig zu verbessern. Weitere Studienziele sind die Validierung der ACR/EULAR Klassifikationskriterien von 2019 an der LüRIgG-4 Kohorte, retrospektive Auswertungen der Therapien, Fragebogen-basierte Erhebung der aktuellen Versorgungssituation sowie der vorliegenden Komorbiditäten und Identifizierung potentieller Biomarker anhand gesammelter Bioproben. Die erste Zwischenauswertung der Patientenfragebögen der LüRIgG-4 Kohorte kann hier in kleinem Auszug präsentiert werden.

## Authors

- Felix Müller (University Hospital Augsburg): corresponding author
- Thea Thiele (Medizinische Hochschule Hannover): h-index 12; 450 citations
- Frank Krämer (University of Augsburg): h-index 28; 3,321 citations
- Désirée Dunstheimer (University Hospital Augsburg): h-index 16; 1,727 citations
- Torsten Witte (Medizinische Hochschule Hannover): h-index 50; 8,944 citations
- Matthias Wahle (University Hospital Augsburg): h-index 16; 632 citations

## Topics

- IgG4-Related and Inflammatory Diseases
- Systemic Sclerosis and Related Diseases
- Interstitial Lung Diseases and Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis

## References

- Zachary Scott Wallace, Ray Naden, Suresh T. Chari, Hyon K. Choi, Emanuel Della‐Torre, Jean‐Francois Dicaire, et al. The 2019 American College of Rheumatology/European League Against Rheumatism Classification Criteria for IgG4‐Related Disease. Arthritis & Rheumatology. 2019;72(1):7-19. doi:10.1002/art.41120.
- John H. Stone, Yoh Zen, Vikram Deshpande. IgG4-Related Disease. New England Journal of Medicine. 2012;366(6):539-551. doi:10.1056/nejmra1104650.
